People say the game is mediocre, and perhaps that is justified. However, I feel the game is at least in the higher end of mediocre games, and can produce a lot of fun. At least for fans of the different creatures the game tried (and in my opinion, succeeded) to bring alive.

I am not in a position to review the multiplayer so consider this to be mainly a single player review.

People are usually concerned with the duration of gameplay, and what many have said is true, it's short, with the marine campaign being the longest, Predator in the middle and the alien the shortest. It's a shame, as I found that the alien was the most fun, then the predator, and lastly the marine. Though this is not to say that it isn't fun to play the marine, it's just the weakest of the species. All three species campaigns adding up to perhaps 12h, though I might be slow - spending a lot of time in the shadows as an alien, watching how the marines patrol, and cloaked as a predator, deciding which marine to pick off first.
What this game has that the earlier AVP games didn't have, was a more polished experience as the different species: 
Aliens feel like more than just a floating camera with floating arms and a tail that shows up every so often. Now you move as your body moves, you can feel with every turn of the camera as your playable xenomorph changes position and sometimes the tail shows up when you turn around fast enough. The way you can leap, look, attack, all are improvements to a first-person-shooter experience of sneaking or leaping and attacking in close quarters, always in the same brutal sense you pick up from the films.
Predators too feel like they move, behave and look like a predator from the movies. There's nothing like re-enacting a scene so reminiscent from the films: Leap up a tree cloaked, observe the marines below, say you want the smart gunner first, you distract the marine with some distorted human cry, wait for them to get closer, then leap (focus+attack1) on them and pick a trophy.
And that brings me to the full-body awareness. It's a small feature, but I still value it when developers pick up on the little things which can mean a lot to make an experience feel just right. the trophy kills and stealth kills seem to have been the baby of the project to hammer out a smooth way to behave with the character, with little distracting buggy animations, if any at all, just going up to a human and impaling them with your tail, literally, or just stabbing an alien with your wristblades, lifting them up in the air, seeing the dangling xeno giving its last painful shriek, then becoming motionless, and you, the predator, just casting it aside.
The story isn't anything new or particularly gripping, but it's okay, and what you could expect, though the AVP2 game had a better story, this game has a better story than the avp movies, so there's that.
If only they'd extended the Predator and Alien campaigns, I think the game would have gained more popularity. Also, since the games are trying to be close to the movies, I think it's time to make the "marine" human character female, if you want to copy some of the defining features of the films. Which isn't bad, just saying.
Graphics do justice to the details of the predators and their swinging dreadlocks, and the shining, slimey aliens, coupled with great animations, which you can admire both while hunting the different species and while playing them, made it a fun experience.
Personally the game didn't suffer from issues (and I have a mediocre laptop, win7, intel dual core 2ghz, 4gRAM, graphics card shares its memory with ram, only 64mb dedicated), only a flickering mouse in the mainmenu. I'm mentioning this because I've seen so many games suffer from multiple bugs, though often repairable, this didn't really have any issues for me.

Lack of survivor maps as a predator or alien felt like the greatest sorrows of missed opportunities for this game (which I think could have been very feasible additions, as I write in a post on the forums of the game here on steam).

This is the 2010 first person shooter video game release based on the Fox movie franchises, Aliens, Predator and Aliens vs Predator. There is a highly acclaimed Aliens vs Predator game already. This is not a remake of that game, but an all new installment with an original (brief) story.

Aliens vs Predator is broken up into three campaigns (it has multiplayer games as well). One campaign you play as the Xenomorph aliens, another you play as the Predator and a third played as a human space marine sent in to combat the two. Each species / character (Predator, Xenomorph, space marine) plays differently. Space marines play like traditional first person shooters, Xenomorphs can climb on the walls and ceilings and use stealth to drop down and kill enemies because they die VERY easily and Predators use a combination of the two. They can jump far distances, stealth kill and change their vision to see in different ways.

As a space marine, there are a few good and useful weapon types, shotgun, pulse rifle, pistol, flame thrower and more. You can carry three weapons at a time, which feels like enough. Shooting as the space marine feels very imprecise, because you can barely see your crosshairs, the enemies move quick and most of the time, you're shooting at black Xenomorphs on dark walls. The game makes use of light and shadows, because it gives you a flashlight and flares. Both the flashlight and flares are limitless and it felt like there should be sparing usage of both. The flashlight can flicker or go out a few seconds. Your enemy radar can cut out for a moment.

Movement and mouse aim feel clunky, slow and sluggish. At least there is a run button for a few moments of speed when running down straight corridors. Speaking of the run button, a lot of times it feels like I can just run through from the enemies instead of dealing with them.

There are in your face moments when you need to melee enemies to get them out of your face. Xenomorphs will pounce on you, face huggers will jump in your face, but not so much that it gets annoying like in other games. You even have some cool melee kills that you can use.

Enemy AI and variety is good, Xenomorphs effortlessly crawl everywhere, they can turn in circles on walls, ceilings, nooks, crannies and eves. Face huggers will avoid your crosshairs, Predators will sniper you and even big lumbering android soldiers take some aim to kill. None of the enemies feel particularly deadly or powerful... just difficult to shoot when compared to other games.

The game sets a great atmosphere that is diverse from section to section. The Xenomorph areas are dark, futuristic and gritty, while the Predator jungles are a foreboding, luscious beauty with a sense of something watching you. The music is good and all background music matches the area.

The only big gripe is the fact that there are level conclusions. The level ends and you are sent to a screen with your score and where to save or continue. This really breaks immersion especially when the next level takes place the moment the last level ended. This should have been made into a seamless transition with no halt in the action. The score could have been shown on screen, auto saved (which the game does autosave) and keep the action going. Even playing audio logs is cumbersome and could have been done much better instead of having to pause the game... find the audio log and then return to the action. There are better ways to do that without taking yourself out of the action. Apparently there are audio logs (and other tedious collectables), it is a shame that system is so cumbersome that I don't care to listen.

There are voices in your head telling you what to do, however they don't sound all that believable for the situation you're supposed to be in. It is like they are too pleasant for a situation that has dozens dying. But perhaps having someone barking orders and yelling at you might not be the best to stay focused.

The objectives are pretty simple and its rinse wash repeat. Go here... clear a wave of enemies... open this door... find the power supply and bring it to a door so you can open it and go through. The level design offers a nice path... going upstairs and downstairs, and weaves around areas, but it is all one way with little chance of getting lost. The game is painfully short with the marine campaign being the longest and taking around 3 hours to complete the first time. It feels more like the campaigns are to teach you everything for multiplayer.

In conclusion, there are better first person shooters out there more worthy of your time, but if you are a big fan of the franchise, you can pick the game up for $5 or cheaper and have hours of fun with it. I keep thinking of ways this game could have been better, such as more variety with what to do. Sentries you can put up yourself. More friendlies to fight along side. A crouch button to crawl through air ducts. More secrets or exploration, because it feels like the game has zero secrets. More situations that require stealth or thought instead of running to fights or from fights. Light and BRIEF turret and or driving sections (Aliens movie had a driving section). Maybe for the sequel...

Aliens vs Predator (2010) is a first person shooter that introduces you to three seperate storylines involving a Human, a Predator, and an Alien. Overall the storylines are decent, while not nearly as difficult as I would have prefered. For example Nightmare Difficulty seems to simply increase the damage and accuracy of your opponents, but not necessarily making them difficult due to one shot mechanics available to Predator and Alien. Boss fights bring a interesting level of difficulty, but are still single meat shields with high health pools that you have to mow down while dodging mechanics and the occassional add. Overall scenary in the game is one of the highest pluses I will give, as the environements truely have the universes feel to them. 

TLDR: Singleplayer 

Scenary and Graphical Immersion: 9/10 

Difficulty: 3/10

Storylines: 6/10

MULTIPLAYER SECTION

If you plan to play the multiplayer on this game this is the section you should read. For those who have played Alien vs Predator (1999) and Alien vs Predator 2 (2001) then the combat of this game is much different as it follows a rock, paper, scissors style of gameplay in melee combat. Both Aliens and Predators can perform Light and Heavy Attacks where the heavy attacks can be interrupted by the light attacks, while  the light attacks can be blocked and countered. Marines can block and light attack to counter. Overall depending on the the skill of the people in game the combat can be quite fast paced, also retaining the executions for both predator and alien, which will one shot from the back, and one shot on low health from a front grab. 

TLDR: MULTIPLAYER

Balance: 6/10 (Before the Alien Wall Tail swipe nerf the balance was horrid. While better, Predators are usually a little overpowered compared to Marine and Alien unless the latters have skill advantage).

Maps: 8/10 (Each map usually feels a little different that others, as well as offering different advantages to each of the species. For Example Pyramid and Alien.)

Community: 5/10 (The game has not aged well due to the lack of modding tools. While there is a community still, there have been many reports of hacking throughout the public games. As such playing with a group of friends privately is preferable.)

Gameplay: 7/10 (The one thing I enjoy about this game is the Alien FEELS like an Alien. Your quick, stealthy, and lethal. The Predator also gives you the feel of hunting the other players while using the advanced tech, and Marine keeps you on your heels trying to watch for pings on your motion tracker. Overall the game feels RIGHT, the only cons are lack of Alien Lifecycle and the Rock Paper Scissors limiting the flow of combat.)

OVERALL I do recommend this game simple for the singleplayer if you love the franchise, however the multiplayer should be stuck to friends only unless you want to risk running into a usual hacker ingame. If possible wait for a sale, which usually brings this game down to under 5$ which is well worth the price.

This is game is a such an underrated gem, so that I don't even know where to start this review. I'm millennial and I know all these movies about Aliens and Predators since my childhood. I didn't play original AvP game by Rebellion because I got my first home PC only in the early 2000s when there was already AvP 2 from Monolith Studios (F) and I still actually remember how cool that game was. I also remember how I learned about this soft-reboot to be released by the makers of the original AvP and how I was hyped about it. But then for some weird reason this game had some mixed reviews upon launch. I played it myself and coudln't understand why. I personally think that this is a very solid title and it had plenty of content for its time. All three campaigns had very different gameplay, and even that they all were played on the same levels, the atmosphere and the work with the setting were just astonishing! Not to mention that it's just super cool to be able to play for xenomorph, Yautja and colonial marine within a single game! And so, just like in AvP 2 we were witnessing a single story from different perspectives and we had to play all three campaigns to completely understand its plot. The game was also inspired by Alien vs Predator 2004 movie and it basically can be counted its proper sequel instead of that terrible thing that we got. Here I would like to also note that when talking about Alien movies, Predator movies and Aliens vs Predator movies, I ignore some of them and to me they are not canon because of personal preferences (I like Alien, Aliens, Predator, Predator 2, Alien vs Predator, Predators, Prey, Alien: Romulus and Predator: Killer of Killers without extended ending. I will decide what I think of Alien: Earth and Predator: Badlands once I watch them. I also count Aliens and Predator franchises as one single universe). So, I ignore AvPR, for example, but I like the 2004 movie and I do not understand all the critics around it. I do think that Paul Anderson actually did pretty good job trying to mix two different kind of horrors from both Alien and Predator series in that film. And so, this game has ancient pyramid build by Yautja just like in the film, the Weyland-Yutani Corparation and their awful actions to control xenomorphs, and, of course, colonial marines and predators who come to clean all the mess. There is also famous Lance Henriksen himself who plays director of Weyland-Yutani (there is an explanation on who Karl Bishop Weyland is and why he looks so much like Charles Bishop Weyland from AvP 2004. The events of 2004 in Bouvetøya, Antarctica, also directly mentioned). This is an old game from 2010, so the graphics might not be what you are used to, but the graphics were pretty great for that time period.  It has a first-person view.  The game has a pretty decent single player campaign, and offers four difficulty levels.  The marine has six scenarios, while the predator and the alien both have five scenarios.  You will do  the single player campaign a total of three times.

You will do it once as a marine, once as a predator, and once as an alien.  Even though you are running around in the same locations with each play-through, it's really cool to see things from the point of view of each species.  Each species have their own goals too, and you come away afterwards realizing that there is no definite good guy or bad guy.  There is only survival of the fittest.

The game does not have any trading cards, but it does have fifty achievements.  If you are an achievement hunter, you will have to do the campaign between six and nine times total, as all three species have achievements for both the Hard and Nightmare difficulties.  There are checkpoints in each scenario, on each difficulty except for Nightmare.  That one has to be totally completed without dying.

The game also has multi-player, both co-op and PVP, in seven different modes.  However, due to the age of the game you might have a little trouble finding people to play with, especially when you are trying to get all the multi-player achievements.  Everybody knows Survivor mode, with it's increasing waves of enemies coming at you.  Many games these days call it Horde mode.

For Infestation mode, everybody starts out as a marine, but after a minute or so the game switches a random person to an alien.  When the alien kills a marine, the marine respawns as an alien.  The last marine standing is the winner.  There are three Death Match modes ([i]individual, mixed species, and species team[/i]), which can be set for a certain time limit or a certain number of kills.

The last two multi-player modes I have not tried yet, so I can not comment on them.  They are Predator Hunt mode, and Domination mode.  Both the co-op and the PVP matches can be played on the various maps from the campaign.  There are also two DLC packs you can buy which offer several more maps.  Some of the multi-player modes limit the number of players in a match, and some don't.

So far the game has run perfectly fine for me.  I have not experienced any bugs or glitches.  However, some other players have reported a few bugs, mainly on newer systems, so you may have a compatibility issue.  Also, some of my friends have had connection issues during multi-player matches.  Who knows though, whether that is due to the game itself, due to the peer-to-peer connection, or due to their own internet.

When it comes to online play, you really can´t go wrong. You can choose between three classes:
Marine, Alien Or Predator.

If you like living with constant dread that someone or something is following you, then Marine is for you.
If you like making people live with constant dread, following them until you eventually end their misery. Then Alien is for you.
If you like striking fear into children and men alike, you are either Dr Disrespect, or any other minecraft youtuber, then the predator is for you (Oh wait.)

There is also a brilliant, fun, and horrifying single player campaign, (horrifying if you play as the marine).
All in all. 
Good game.

Then it falls flat and turns cliche. Alien and Predator campaigns are still okay because it's fun to play as those characters - to jump around, get on the walls, try various Predator weapons, etc.

The good sides are very nice graphics and atmosphere, the maps are well made (though there are too few of them in my opinion) the music is fitting and it's a great experience to play as marine, alien or predator.

The game is fun, but nothing more.

But, it usually just become either holding down the trigger or mashing the melee button until your enemy stops moving. "Brutal" kills (for predator and alien) are, as you'd expect, brutal and viseral. However, I don't understand why the developers thought it was necessary for have these lengthy, uninterruptible kill animations when you perform a stealth kill, where enemies can spot you and shoot you while your still going through the animation. This especially becomes annoying in the alien campaign where your weak health forces you to be stealthy.

4. Single-player: There are 3 campaigns: alien, predator, and marine. 
Marine is the lengthiest yet perhaps the most boring of the two. It starts of with a survival-esque horror feel, but quickly devolves into a gun-ho action game where aliens are more of an annoyance than a threat. The story itself is nothing inspiring as it follows the same beats you'd expect from an alien film. 
Alien and Predator are both more interesting than their marine counterparts as their gameplay is more unique than the standard "go here and shoot the things." Alien is the most challenging of the three as it enforces stealth gameplay as previously mentioned, and despite its flaws and lack of interesting plot, I found this campaign the most enjoyable. Predator is good all-around as you have to adapt your approach from stealth to vigorous melee-button mashing when you face marines and/or xenomorphs. The story, although nothing reward winning, is competent and maintains your interest.

Multiplayer: As you'd expect from a game of this age, the player base is very limited; still, you'll probably find at least one full server of players. Of course, whether you'd enjoy it is a different matter. The fact is, that this game's multiplayer is horrendously un-balanced, specificall when it comes to the predators. Predators have the strongest melee attacks, best gadgets, can move fast, cloak, and can easily spot aliens and marines thanks to their all-seeing vision filters. With this in mind, its no surprise in species free-for-alls (and teams) everyone picks predators, no one picks marines, and only the brave or morbidly curious will pick the aliens. The only redeemable game modes are Predator-Hunt where its one predator vs everyone else who are marines; and infestation, where an alien must infect (kill) marines to convert them to his side and win the game.

Overall: The game is decent. Clearly, it was made by people who liked the universe, but their passion doesn't exacly make me ignore its several flaws. I place it at a 6/10. (5 being mediocre)

I'm not going to lie, the AvP crossover franchise is one of the coolest things our planet has ever been blessed with, so I am going into this with a shade of fanboyism. All things considered, this game isn't bad, but it's a huge step back compared to the classic AvP games.

First of all, for a game from 2010, it still looks stunning thanks to the Asura engine. The texturework, lighting and animations are all superb, polished and you can tell the people making the visuals had a LOT of love for the source material. The sound design is also pretty good and it's true to the movies and previous games. The voice acting sadly ranges from mega-cringe to average. All of the marines sound like a reading of an edgy highschool freshman drama, and the writing isn't really Oscar material either.

As with previous titles, there are three campaigns: Alien, Marine and Predator. 
The Marine is your standard FPS campaign and the franchise's well-known weapons like the Pulse Rifle, Flamethrower and Smart Gun all make a return. I just wish the balancing and damage made more sense. The Pulse Rifle is laughably weak and it should never, ever take 40-50 rounds to take out one single Xeno. The Smart gun isn't much better either and ammo for it is scarce, not to mention you only really get to use it twice! The Sniper is totally overpowered and I ended up just running around with that, since you can no-scope to your heart's content and a headshot is an instant kill. The shotgun is pretty rad, at least.
The Alien campaign is all about sneaking and ambushes, and to be honest, it was the least memorable of the bunch.
The Predator campaign is what you'd expect, gadgets and stealth-domination, and it would've been glorious if they didn't give you all the cool toys in the last 40 minutes of the game. You don't really get to play around too much. But when you do, it's still pretty darn satisfying to leap around cloaked and take out fools without the rest realizing you're picking them off one by one. I'd say out of the three, this one was my favourite.

From the above, and my playtime, you can also gather that the game is pretty short. And I kind of even took my time. The Marine and Predator campaigns are about 2 hours each, and the Alien is about an hour long. Now I'm not a huge fan of games that artificially extend the playtime for no good reason, but this is really, really not a lot of content and I'd imagine someone who paid 60 bucks for this at release would've been ticked off. This short length wouldn't be a problem if the game didn't literally recycle all of its levels throughout the three campaigns one-to-one - while this is the only game this kind of laziness could get a pass since it's the whole "one story from three different points of view" shebang, but even here, it's just pathetically copy-pasted. I'm not even going to mention the story because there really isn't one. Go here, do that, stop Weyland (again), nothing at all to make me care about what's going on.

I've dinged this title a bit already, but let me mention the biggest problem I had with the game. This game was probably made (or was commissioned by) filmmakers, because there are stupid kill animations all over the place for the Alien and Predator. Even on a game this short, you'll spend a lot of time staring at finishing moves, and you're vulnerable and completely helpless during these to boot. Anyone who had a problem with Glory Kills in DOOM 2016/Eternal should go play this game and realize just how bad this kind of system is, especially on bossfights with Xeno enemies or when playing as a Xeno. It's hard to be stealthy and agile when you finally isolate an enemy and it takes up to 5 seconds to finish them, which is plenty of time for a guard to see you or stroll around the corner. They're cool when you see them the first three times, but by the end, they just become tedious and annoying.

To sum up, I'd say if you're a fan of the franchise, give it a shot, but definitely get it as cheap as humanly possible (definitely not worth more than 10€, if that) - it's laughably short and the worst part is that length wouldn't be a problem if the game actually let you use the stuff it gives you in the last minute for one or two levels more. It just kind of feels like a demo to something bigger, just a big tease. The annoying animations aside, it's still a very good looking and sounding game and I'd be lying if the AvP fan in me didn't have a few giddy moments ripping out spines and chomping Marines with a Xeno. It's okay if you have an afternoon or two to kill and you want some Xeno-killing action, just don't expect too much.

The Aliens and Predator franchises have had there ups downs, and when combined into films it was the ladder. In gaming however they really worked! Starting back in the Arcade as a “Final Fight” style beat-em up, the Atari Jaguar in 1994, the PC version in 2000, and a sequel in 2004. All were fun games for their time. So how does the latest in the series hold up? Well it helps if your a fan of Alien, and The Predator movies, and I am so my review may be biased. The game is broken into three campaigns that tie in the main story. Players can choose a Colonial Marine, the Alien, or The Predator. Each class plays very unique with their own abilities. I really wish they added “Aim Down Sites”. Firing from the hip in gaming is just old school, I need my sites! Second complaint is the motion tracker, It's all but useless in the game. I know I'll get some heat for saying this, but Aliens Colonial Marines made far better use of the motion tracker.  My second favorite campaign was The Predator. With all of his tools at your disposal, you will feel like an unstoppable hunter. My only complaint on The Predator is the “pred jump”. At times it can be a pain to line up, but once you know the map its less frustrating. The Aliens campaign was my least favorite. The Alien can transition to walls, and run in 3D. It has some interesting fatalities, and is extremely fast. This could have been easily fixed if the Alien had 3rd person perspective. The game offers a decent amount of multiplayer modes, and a decent number of maps. The only thing I wish is there was a little more variety in the scenery. Your either in a Jungle, or a pyramid, and that’s about it.  The game will run on almost any PC if you adjust the resolution, and graphics options (Not your Apple II, but anything from 2010 and up should be fine). Overall this game despite its flaws is a very fun play, and I recommend it. If you've been passing on this one, and your a fan of either franchise you should pick it up. First time playing Aliens vs Predator from 2010 (also known as AvP 3) and I was really hype about it.

The concept is cool, playing with or against well known horror aliens like the xenomorph or the predator, also adding humans into the mix is a cool idea. Graphics for its time are alright, especially the lighting and the shadow effects. The game contains multiple campaigns where you can play with all factions, all of them play differently, which is interesting to have. Every campaign has some kind of collectibles as well and the game has achievements to complete. The sound design and the soundtrack is really fitting to AvP. The game also tries to be authentic to the Alien and Predator movies, some moments from the game trying to replicate scenes from said movies, and I think the fans can appreciate these. Each campaign has their iconic equipment to use and areas to play in. When it was active, the multiplayer was considered to be great in this game.

But in my opinion this game has some issues which just makes the product hard to enjoy. If you have played through the marine campaign, you basically saw all of the maps in the single player, because the other campaigns play on the same maps as the marine campaign. Then, for me the game was too dark and this was especially annoying with the marines. The game in general is hard, even on medium difficulty can give you a hard time, although there are exceptions to note here, which I will talk about later. The story for each campaign was not interesting for me at all even though it covers most aspects of the universe and tries to show some kind of the plot, but with no avail, the voice acting also was questionable at times. The control scheme was a struggle to get used to it. The playtime of each campaign is short, the longest one is the marine campaign with it's 2-3 hours length, the predator campaign takes 1-1 and half hour to beat and the alien one is just less than an hour long.

I played all campaigns on hard difficulty and they have their own pros and cons as well...

[b]Marine campaign[/b]
This one actually starts out well, the horror factor is noticeable in the first few levels and story wise it has a good introduction, but these disappears later. This is one of the hardest campaigns in this game and in my opinion the least enjoyable as well. Maps are too dark for the marines even with flashlight and flares, making the aliens hard to detect. Enemies here are annoying to fight against, especially the xenomorphs and the androids which gave me a headache, thanks to the marines' sluggish movements which makes you an easy target and barely can make you dodge attacks. Speaking of sluggish movements, some maps has big areas to cover and because of this it can take minutes to go on foot, giving you some down time. Melee system is just useless to have for this faction.

I can understand that in AvP the marines are the weakest faction, so they should have the most difficult campaign as well with their difficulties which makes the game somewhat authentic, but honestly this was just not fun to play through.

[b]Predator campaign[/b]
Comparing to the marine, the predator has enjoyable abilities and equipments gameplay wise, it also has an interesting looking melee system which work like as a rock-paper-scissors game, and the visual representation in the HUD and the appearance of the predator works well and makes it distinguishable from the other factions. However, this campaign is highly dependent on the player's ability to understand this character, because even though the game gives you a tutorial level, the first few levels are going to be difficult if you can't understand the tutorial and use it in action. Personally, this was more annoying at first then the marine campaign in general, but after a lot of trial and error I got used to it, especially when you realize that you want to avoid confrontation with the enemies and try to separate them as much as possible, and I can say that this campaign is much easier than the marine one. The melee system which seems interesting gets annoying to use, because on higher difficulty I was barely able to kill anyone with it, and in the end you will going to use one or two equipment and just cheese your way through of everything.

If you can get used to the predator playstyle I think this campaign can be alright, but the playtime it's still short and the first few levels are still hell to get through, but this is miles better than the marine campaign.

[b]Alien campaign[/b]
This campaign is similar to the Predator one, but with less equipment to use. It's also somewhat heavy on melee combat but it's more about executing enemies from behind. Once again the HUD and visual representation is different from what we saw so far and the difficulty is pretty alright here, except in the last boss fight which is a bit hard mainly because you don't know how to deal with the enemy. Xenomorph's movement is pretty cool, as you can move on walls and go in vents, but sometimes certain areas don't connect well and you can't really chain these movements together. 

This is definitely the highlight of the game, however as I wrote before it's the shortest one as well. This gives some decent fun.

[b]Verdict[/b]
I'm not a big AvP or Aliens or Predator fan and since the public multiplayer is not active and you can only play it with friends, I can only go by the campaigns and to be honest it was a mixed experience. I can recommend playing this only if you are either a fan or you want to play something difficult, otherwise I would skip it. 15€ is a lot for it, but around 5-7€ is a good price to pay.

You have the chance to play as marine, alien, and predator and although the story line in each campaign is independent of the others they do exist within the same story arc. The marine campaign is the most challenging, as you often feel underpowered against the aliens, but it’s not frustrating and this vulnerability certainly adds to the already considerable tension. Playing as an alien can be disorientating at times and the movement system takes some getting used to but it’s worth it for the fun to be had stalking the marines and scientists. Playing as a predator, although still enjoyable, was not quite as much fun, and I found the gameplay and combat systems in this campaign less convincing than in the others. The atmosphere throughout is impressive and the graphics are good (although some animations are a little muddy in colour). The voice acting is also good, which helps to add to the compelling atmosphere. It isn’t a long game (I took my time, but still completed the three campaigns in about 15 hours) and the multiplayer seems pretty much dead (I did manage a few games, but only with friends) but if you can get it on sale, as I did, it’s well worth a few quid. Despite its flaws this game successfully recreates the atmosphere and edginess of the movies and should not disappoint fans of the two franchises. 4/5

Aliens vs. Predator (2010) - In-Depth Review
Overview: Released by Rebellion Developments, Aliens vs. Predator (2010) revitalizes the iconic franchise by offering players the chance to experience the intense combat between three distinct species: the Colonial Marines, Aliens, and Predators. Each faction provides unique gameplay mechanics and storylines, creating a rich and engaging experience for fans of the franchise.

Graphics and Sound: The game's graphics were a standout feature at the time of release. The environments are meticulously designed, capturing the dark, foreboding atmosphere of the Aliens and Predator films. Character models are impressively detailed, especially the iconic Aliens and Predators, which faithfully reflect their cinematic counterparts.

Sound design plays a crucial role in immersion, with chilling sound effects that heighten tension and a haunting score that evokes the themes of the movies. The authentic sounds of the iconic motion tracker and the visceral effects of combat add to the authenticity, making players feel they are truly part of the universe.

Gameplay: Aliens vs. Predator features three distinct campaigns, each offering unique gameplay experiences:

Colonial Marines: The human perspective provides a more traditional shooter experience, emphasizing tactics and teamwork. Players utilize an array of weapons, from pulse rifles to flamethrowers, while navigating dark corridors filled with tension and uncertainty. The campaign is marked by intense moments, especially when facing the Aliens, requiring players to be strategic in their approach.

Aliens: Playing as the Alien is a thrilling experience, focusing on agility and stealth. The ability to crawl on walls and ceilings creates dynamic gameplay, allowing for unexpected ambushes. The Alien's unique movement and attack mechanics provide a fresh contrast to the slower, more methodical approach of the Marines.

Predators: The Predator campaign emphasizes stealth and strategy. Players can use cloaking devices, advanced technology, and brutal close-combat moves to take down foes. The variety of weapons, from the iconic wrist blades to the devastating plasma caster, allows for creative approaches to each encounter.

The multiplayer component adds immense replay value, offering various modes such as deathmatch and domination. Players can engage in fierce battles, with the unique abilities of each species providing diverse strategies. However, the online connectivity issues have plagued the game, making matchmaking frustrating at times and detracting from the overall experience. Players often faced lag and disconnections, which diminished the excitement of competitive play.

Narrative and Atmosphere: The storytelling is woven through the campaigns, connecting the three perspectives in a cohesive narrative that honors the lore of both franchises. While the plot may not be groundbreaking, it effectively captures the essence of Aliens and Predator, delivering a sense of urgency and danger throughout.

The atmosphere is palpable, with tension building through the use of lighting, sound, and environmental storytelling. The game masterfully recreates the eerie and oppressive settings from the films, immersing players in the rich lore of the AVP universe.

Weaknesses: Despite its strengths, the game is not without flaws. Some players reported issues with AI behavior, particularly in the Alien and Marine campaigns, where enemies could be unresponsive or predictable. Additionally, certain multiplayer modes suffered from balance issues, leading to frustration among players.

The lack of post-launch content and updates limited the game's longevity, leaving a passionate community yearning for more. Moreover, the connectivity issues made online play inconsistent, creating an obstacle for players eager to engage in multiplayer matches. A more robust support system from the developers could have addressed some of these gameplay imbalances and bugs, ultimately enhancing the experience.

Conclusion: Aliens vs. Predator (2010) stands as a remarkable entry in the franchise, successfully blending thrilling gameplay, impressive graphics, and an immersive atmosphere. While it has its shortcomings, particularly in connectivity, the game remains a beloved title for fans and a testament to the potential of the AVP universe. With continued support and a dedicated community, there is hope for the resurgence of this iconic series. Let's rally behind this game and keep the AVP legacy alive!
